answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices ensure Sybil resistance by imposing a strict negative expected payoff for identity multiplication, thereby dissuading reef-like duplication. In adversarial environments, these mechanisms converge to a Nash equilibrium where rational agents cannot profitably engage in Sybil attacks; any attempt at such multiplication results in a punitive cascade, akin to a harsh penalty for breaching agreements at a wharf, deterring whisper networks from benefiting through false identities.
